studies.title: [Intersection of gender, working conditions, and caregiving burden in post-COVID-19 syndrome: A cross-sectional mixed-methods study among healthcare workers].
studies.authors: Antonietti, Laura, Straw, Cecilia, Riveiro, Manuel, Martínez, María José et al.
studies.abstract: Post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) among healthcare personnel impacts quality of life and work performance negatively, and is associated with gender and work conditions. The study aimed to characterize PCS in healthcare personnel and explore their perceptions regarding gender conditions, work, and caregiving burden. Between May and October 2023, a cross-sectional mixed-methods study was conducted in health professionals with a history of COVID-19 who worked in Buenos Aires City and Buenos Aires Province. PCS was defined as the persistence of symptoms for more than one month. Using nonprobability snowball sampling strategy, an anonymous survey was conducted on clinical, sociodemographic, occupational, gender, and caregiving variables, along with individual and group interviews. The information was analyzed according to the Ecological and Social Framework. A total of 444 surveys and 22 interviews were analyzed. The overall prevalence of PCS was 57%, with a higher frequency and number of symptoms in women, a finding that remained consistent when disaggregated by profession. In the multivariate analysis, female gender, non-permanent employment, the number of COVID-19 episodes, and the perception of a heavier domestic workload were associated with a higher likelihood of PCS. The qualitative component revealed an unequal distribution of caregiving responsibilities, a greater mental burden on women, work overload, and limited institutional support. The findings suggest that clinical experience of PCS among healthcare workers is situated at the intersection of gender, work, and caregiving distribution. This approach can guide future research and generate hypotheses for preventive and healthcare-worker support policies in the face of future emergencies. Introducción: El síndrome post-COVID-19 (SPC) en personal de salud impacta en peor calidad de vida y menor desempeño laboral, y se asocia con condiciones de género y trabajo. El estudio buscó caracterizar el SPC en profesionales de salud y explorar sus percepciones respecto de condiciones de género, trabajo y carga de cuidado. Materiales y métodos: Entre mayo y octubre de 2023 se realizó un estudio transversal de métodos mixtos en profesionales de salud con antecedente de COVID-19 que trabajaban en Ciudad y Provincia de Buenos Aires. Se consideró SPC la persistencia de síntomas mayor a un mes. Mediante muestreo no probabilístico, se realizó una encuesta anónima sobre variables clínicas, sociodemográficas, laborales de género y cuidados, y entrevistas individuales y grupales. La información se analizó según el Modelo Ecológico y Social. Resultados: Se analizaron 444 encuestas y 22 entrevistas. La prevalencia global de SPC fue 57%, con mayor frecuencia y número de síntomas en mujeres, que se mantuvo al desagregar por profesión. En el análisis multivariado, el género femenino, la contratación no permanente, la cantidad de episodios de COVID-19 y la percepción de mayor carga de trabajo doméstico se asociaron con mayor probabilidad de SPC. El componente cualitativo mostró distribución desigual del cuidado, mayor carga mental en mujeres, sobrecarga laboral y escasa contención institucional. Conclusión: Los hallazgos sugieren que el SPC en personal de salud se inscribe en la intersección entre género, trabajo y organización del cuidado. Este enfoque puede orientar futuras investigaciones y generar hipótesis para políticas preventivas y de cuidado ante futuras emergencias.

studies.title: [An insight into the long/post COVID care situation in Germany-a rapid scoping review].
studies.authors: Ebster, Marlene, Gscheidle, Sonja, Lange, Saskia, Weijburg, Thomas et al.
studies.abstract: Long/post COVID and related conditions such as myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome, postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome and post-vaccination syndrome are associated with persistent functional impairments and are met with care structures in Germany that are difficult to navigate. The rapid scoping review offers an insight into care structures, capacities, access, care pathways and gaps in care for these patient groups in the German healthcare system. It also takes into account patient and care provider perspectives. The study follows the recommendations of the Joanna Briggs Institute and the PRISMA ScR checklist for conducting (rapid) scoping reviews. A MEDLINE search was conducted from 2020 onwards with predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria for evidence sources related to care in Germany. 44 evidence sources were included. General practitioners and paediatricians act as the first point of contact. Specialised outpatient clinics and rehabilitation facilities take on complex diagnostics and patient treatment. Care networks are rare. Navigating the healthcare system is characterised by information gaps, unclear responsibilities and long waiting times, so that those affected often organise their own care. Some report stigmatisation, misdiagnoses and stressful activation recommendations despite the risk of post exertional malaise. Care is unevenly accessible, poorly coordinated and only limitedly evidence based. Shared knowledge and case databases, training, better diagnostic tools and robust efficacy studies are needed to improve access, management and safety of long/post COVID care. HINTERGRUND: Long/Post COVID und verwandte Krankheitsbilder wie Myalgische Enzephalomyelitis/Chronisches Fatigue Syndrom, Posturales Orthostatisches Tachykardiesyndrom (POTS) und Postvakzinierungssyndrom gehen mit anhaltenden Funktionseinschränkungen einher und treffen auf schwer überschaubare Versorgungsstrukturen. ZIEL: Der Rapid Scoping Review bietet einen Einblick in Versorgungsstrukturen, Kapazitäten, Zugänge und Versorgungslücken für diese Patientengruppen im deutschen Gesundheitssystem. Dabei werden auch die Perspektiven von Leistungserbringenden und Betroffenen berücksichtigt. Die Arbeit folgt den Empfehlungen des Joanna Briggs Institute und der PRISMA-ScR-Checkliste zur Durchführung von (Rapid) Scoping Reviews. Es erfolgte eine MEDLINE-Suche ab 2020 mit vordefinierten Ein- und Ausschlusskriterien für Evidenzquellen mit Bezug zur Versorgung in Deutschland. Es wurden 44 Quellen eingeschlossen. Haus- und kinderärztliche Praxen fungieren als erste Anlaufstelle. Spezialisierte Ambulanzen und Rehabilitationseinrichtungen übernehmen komplexe Diagnostik und Patientenbehandlung. Versorgungsnetzwerke sind selten. Die Navigation von Betroffenen durch das Gesundheitswesen ist von Informationslücken, unklaren Zuständigkeiten und langen Wartezeiten geprägt, sodass diese ihre Versorgung häufig selbst organisieren. Betroffene berichten teilweise von Stigmatisierung, Fehldiagnosen und belastenden Aktivierungsempfehlungen trotz des Risikos einer Post-Exertionellen Malaise. Die Versorgung ist ungleich zugänglich, wenig koordiniert und nur begrenzt evidenzbasiert. Gemeinsame Wissens- und Falldatenbanken, Fortbildungen, bessere diagnostische Instrumente und robuste Wirksamkeitsstudien sind erforderlich, um Zugang, Steuerung und Sicherheit der Long/Post COVID-Versorgung zu verbessern.

studies.title: Dysregulated complement activation in COVID-19: The Role of Soluble Complement Inhibitors.
studies.authors: van der Meulen, Stef, Wang, Haiyu, Nugteren, Saskia, Ponchel, Frederique et al.
studies.abstract: In viral infections, complement activation can contribute to viral clearance, but excessive activation, as observed in severe COVID-19, may drive immunopathology. While much is known about complement-activating factors in COVID-19, insight into the role of endogenous complement inhibitors remains limited. We performed a longitudinal analysis within the BEAT-COVID cohort, comprising hospitalized patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) or ward, and age-matched healthy controls. Serum levels of the complement activation marker soluble membrane attack complex (sC5b-9) and soluble inhibitors C1-Inhibitor (C1-INH), C4b-Binding Protein (C4BP), Factor H, and Factor I were measured by ELISA. In vitro endothelial complement sensitivity was assessed by flow cytometry. Soluble inhibitors were also measured in a cohort of patients with long COVID. Patients admitted to the ICU showed elevated sC5b-9 levels compared to patients admitted to the ward and controls, correlating with disease severity, length of hospitalization, and need for mechanical ventilation, but not mortality. Unexpectedly, levels of all soluble complement inhibitors were elevated, particularly in patients admitted to the ICU. Factor H levels positively correlated with sC5b-9. Endothelial cells pre-incubated with serum from patients admitted to the ICU became more susceptible to complement attack. In patients with long COVID, Factor H and C4BP levels remained elevated compared to pre-pandemic healthy controls. Severe COVID-19 is characterized by extensive complement activation despite elevated circulating inhibitor levels, suggesting impaired local complement regulation at the cell surface, potentially amplified by overwhelming systemic activation, rather than inhibitor deficiency.

studies.title: Potential Physiological Convergence Between GLP-1 Receptor Signaling and Hepatocyte TAZ in Metabolic Liver Disease: From Metabolic Homeostasis to Fibrotic Remodeling.
studies.authors: Gholam, Mohammed F
studies.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) progresses when nutrient excess, insulin resistance, adipose dysfunction, and hepatocellular stress overwhelm hepatic adaptation. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) improve weight, glycemic control, and steatohepatitis, and semaglutide has demonstrated histological improvement in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). In parallel, the transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ; WWTR1) has emerged as a nutrient-, cholesterol-, and mechanics-responsive regulator linking stressed hepatocytes to inflammation and fibrogenesis through Hippo-YAP/TAZ signaling and Indian hedgehog. This narrative review integrates incretin physiology with cell-specific TAZ biology across the gut-brain-axis, adipose tissue, pancreatic islets, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, hepatocytes, immune cells, and hepatic stellate cells. Recent evidence that semaglutide can signal through intrahepatic sinusoidal endothelial GLP-1 receptors provides a weight-loss-independent route to reduced hepatic inflammation and fibrosis; however, it does not establish that TAZ is a downstream mediator. The evidence therefore supports a multilevel convergence model in which GLP-1RAs lower metabolic and inflammatory inputs that favor TAZ activation, while direct GLP-1RA-to-TAZ signaling remains a testable hypothesis. Receptor-validated, cell-specific, weight-controlled, and longitudinal human studies are needed to distinguish mediation from parallel response and to determine whether TAZ-pathway biomarkers can guide mechanism-based therapy.

studies.title: Pancreatic cancer cell and stellate cell-derived exosome crosstalk mediates pancreatic cancer-related diabetes.
studies.journal: Pancreatology : official journal of the International Association of Pancreatology (IAP) ... [et al.]
studies.authors: Sarkar, Rohit, Perera, Chamini J, Hossain, Md J, Tyma, Victoria et al.
studies.abstract: Diabetes is a known risk factor, and a distinct form termed pancreatic cancer-related diabetes (PCRD) often precedes the diagnosis of cancer by 3-5 years, offering a potential window for intervention. We hypothesised that interactions between stromal pancreatic stellate cells (PSCs) and cancer cells trigger secretion of exosomal factors that impair islet function and insulin signalling, contributing to PCRD pathogenesis. KC (KrasLSL-G12D/+; Pdx1-Cre) mice were fed a high-fructose diet (HFrD) or control diet for 16 weeks. Exosomes were isolated from monocultures and co-cultures of cancer/PanIN cells with PSCs, characterised by nanoparticle tracking analysis and transmission electron microscopy, and incubated with mouse β-cells (MIN6) and peripheral cells (hepatocytes, adipocytes, skeletal myocytes). Effects on insulin secretion and insulin-signalling factors were examined. Exosomal glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) expression was modulated by siRNA to assess functional impact. HFrD induced marked glucose intolerance in KC mice and was accompanied by enhanced PSC activation, macrophage infiltration, inflammation, and accelerated PanIN progression. Exosomes from PSCs, cancer cells, and co-cultures displayed typical morphology and marker expression and were efficiently internalised by β-cells and hepatocytes. Functionally, exosomes significantly impaired glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in mouse and human β-cells without altering insulin content. In hepatocytes, PSC-, cancer-, and co-culture-derived exosomes reduced key insulin-signalling components, including IR, IRS, AKT, FOXO1 and GLUT2, and inhibited glucose uptake. Silencing exosomal G6PD partially restored hepatocyte insulin signalling. This study identifies a potential contributor to PCRD and suggests a possible mechanistic role for exosomal G6PD in impaired insulin signalling associated with PCRD.

studies.title: Environmental Factors Associated with Long COVID Severity: A Lifelines Cohort Analysis.
studies.authors: Holtjer, J C S, Thio, C H L, Bloemsma, L D, Maitland-Van der Zee, A H et al.
studies.abstract: Environmental components of the external exposome may influence the severity of long COVID, but population-based studies integrating multiple exposures remain scarce. To identify specific environmental factors most strongly associated with long COVID severity, measured as fatigue, quality of life (QoL), and number of symptoms, within a population-based sample of individuals with self-reported long COVID, and to compare results across multiple statistical approaches. We analyzed data from 1,108 participants in the Lifelines COVID-19 cohort who had self-reported long COVID and had complete covariate information. Outcome information was obtained through questionnaires, and environmental exposures were estimated by geocoded linkage to participant's residential addresses. Analyses were stratified by sex due to large differences in outcome distribution. Exposure-outcome associations were estimated using traditional regression models, horseshoe regression, Bayesian Model Averaging, and Random Forest, with adjustment for age, BMI, and education level. In secondary analyses we further stratified for urbanicity and severity of complaints. Findings varied across analytical methods. The most consistent associations were observed in men: higher neighborhood prevalence of low-income residents was associated with greater fatigue, represented by lower scores (B=-2.09), and greater distance to blue space was associated with lower QoL, represented by higher scores (B=0.26). We did not find any associations in females, or the number of present symptoms in either males or females. The secondary analyses showed differences between urban and rural populations for all outcomes, and when comparing the most fatigued and worst QoL (75 In this study, we found modest and context-dependent associations between certain urban features of the external exposome, particularly neighborhood socioeconomic status and access to blue space, and dimensions of long COVID severity. The heterogeneity of results across sex, urbanicity, and analytical methods highlights the need for targeted follow-up studies in diverse populations.

studies.title: Viral Respiratory Infections: COVID-19.
studies.authors: Naik, Heli
studies.abstract: On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic. By late 2024, COVID-19 had become endemic, with regional surges caused by new variants and declining population immunity. Case fatality rates have decreased because of vaccination and the emergence of less virulent variants, but long COVID persists as a public health concern. Because of structural issues, including those related to employment, housing, health care access, and mistrust, minority and low-income individuals are at higher risk for COVID-19 infection and mortality. Preventive strategies include shared decision-making about vaccination for individuals 6 months and older, two vaccine doses for adults 65 and older, and vaccination for pregnant and breastfeeding individuals. COVID-19 can be distinguished from influenza and respiratory syncytial virus infection through testing. Rapid antigen tests are faster but less sensitive than polymerase chain reaction tests. Outpatient care of COVID-19 focuses on symptomatic relief and early antiviral use when indicated. Inpatient treatment involves remdesivir, corticosteroids, interleuken-6 inhibitors, anticoagulation, and respiratory support. Long-term complications of COVID-19 include cardiovascular, pulmonary, neurologic, mental health, and renal conditions. Thrombotic risk peaks during acute infection and remains elevated for up to 1 year. An effective community response to COVID-19 requires equitable vaccine access, integrated care, and rebuilding of patient trust to counter misinformation.

studies.title: Clinical-functional vulnerability, but not oxidative stress markers, is associated with self-perceived post-COVID sequelae in community-dwelling older adults: a six-month longitudinal study.
studies.journal: Anais da Academia Brasileira de Ciencias
studies.authors: Maia, Railla S, Mastella, Moisés Henrique, Azzolin, Vitória F, Silva, Iana F DA et al.
studies.abstract: Oxidative stress has been proposed as a central mechanism in post-COVID condition pathophysiology; however, its relationship with subjective symptom burden in older adults remains uncertain. This longitudinal study investigated whether oxidative stress markers are associated with self-perceived postCOVID sequelae in community-dwelling older adults over six months. Fifty-five individuals with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection were included, and 49 had complete laboratory data. Hematological, biochemical, and oxidative stress markersincluding thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), protein carbonylation, and DCFH-DA derived reactive oxygen species (ROS)were assessed at baseline and six months. Self-perceived sequelae were measured using a Likert scale, and clinical-functional vulnerability was evaluated with the IVCF-20. Over time, TBARS levels increased and protein carbonylation decreased, while ROS levels remained stable. Some biochemical markers showed significant variation, although mean values remained within reference ranges. No significant associations were observed between oxidative stress markers and self-perceived post-COVID impact. In contrast, greater clinical-functional vulnerability, particularly memory-related domains, was significantly associated with increased perceived burden. Most oxidative changes occurred independently of classical risk factors such as age, sex, diabetes, and obesity. These findings suggest that subjective post-COVID impact in older adults is more strongly related to cognitive and functional vulnerability than to persistent systemic oxidative imbalance.

studies.title: Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) are associated with distinct clinical phenotypes two years after SARS-CoV-2 infection: A data-driven approach.
studies.authors: Verfaillie, Sander C J, Verveen, Anouk, Visser, Denise, Nieuwkerk, Pythia et al.
studies.abstract: It is important to determine whether the persistent cognitive and fatigue complaints, as part of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), are associated with underlying patterns and specific symptoms clusters. Therefore, the aim of the present study was to investigate symptom clusters and clinical phenotypes in PASC. We included n = 153 individuals (53 years old, 66% female, 2 years post SARS-CoV-2 infection) categorized into groups with (n = 88) and without (n = 65) PASC, defined by severe fatigue and concentration problems using validated cut-offs. Symptom clusters (i.e., component loadings and component scores) were identified using principal component analyses (PCA, eigenvalue[EV]>1.0), using clinical, somatic, coping and sleep factors, symptom severity, neuropsychological and physical tests (totalling 19 tests and questionnaires). We then used logistic regression techniques on (participant-level) component scores (standardized) to investigate associations with PASC. Finally, K-means clustering methods to identify clinical phenotypes. Analyses were adjusted for age, sex, education, nationality and time since infection. PCA identified 5 components, explaining 70% of the variance. We labelled these components as follows: (1) PEM, ME/CFS and sleep symptoms, coping factors (EV = 7.0, 36.9% variance), (2) information-processing speed (EV = 2.5, 13.3%), (3) executive functioning (EV = 1.5, 8.0%, (4) physical performance (EV = 1.2, 6.5%), (5) somatic comorbidities and hospital admission (EV = 1.0, 5.5%). Logistic regression showed that only the first component scores (Odds ratio [95% confidence interval] = 97.1 [16.5-570.3], p < 0.001,), and none of the others (all p > 0.05), associated with PASC. Cluster analysis revealed two distinct clinical phenotypes among individuals with severe chronic fatigue: one marked by physical impairment and the other by diminished cognitive performance. Consistent with existing literature, we confirmed that PASC is a heterogeneous syndrome marked by extensive, interrelated symptoms. Notably, we identified specific cognitive and physical clinical phenotypes. These findings are important for future targeted diagnosis and treatment.

studies.title: Octreotide attenuates pancreatic fibrosis through modulation of the HMGB1-Wnt/β-catenin axis in experimental chronic pancreatitis.
studies.authors: Lu, Wenyi, Huang, Shungen, Wang, Jian, Wan, Peng et al.
studies.abstract: Chronic pancreatitis is a progressive fibroinflammatory disease in which activated pancreatic stellate cells and extracellular matrix deposition drive irreversible tissue remodeling. Octreotide has anti-secretory and anti-inflammatory properties, but its anti-fibrotic mechanism remains unclear. To determine whether octreotide attenuates DBTC-induced pancreatic fibrosis through suppression of high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) and downstream Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Male Sprague-Dawley rats received dibutyltin dichloride (DBTC, 7 mg/kg) to induce chronic pancreatitis and were assigned to seven groups (n = 10/group) comprising untreated controls, DBTC model rats, and DBTC rats treated with octreotide alone or in combination with HMGB1 overexpression, HMGB1 knockdown, a vector control, or pharmacological Wnt/β-catenin activation. Octreotide was administered at 10 µg/kg/day for 21 days. Pancreatic injury, collagen deposition, stellate cell activation, HMGB1 inflammatory signaling, and Wnt/β-catenin activity were assessed by biochemical assays, histology, hydroxyproline measurement, immunofluorescence, Western blotting, qPCR, and ELISA. DBTC caused weight loss, pancreatic atrophy, elevated amylase/lipase, severe collagen accumulation, and marked increases in collagen I, α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), HMGB1, TLR4/RAGE, phospho-NF-κB p65, inflammatory cytokines, active/nuclear β-catenin, Wnt1, phospho-GSK3β, Axin2, c-Myc, and Cyclin D1 (all p < 0.0001 vs. Control). Octreotide substantially reversed these changes, halving fibrosis and hydroxyproline content and suppressing HMGB1 translocation/release (all p < 0.0001 vs. Model). HMGB1 overexpression weakened, whereas HMGB1 knockdown mimicked, octreotide-mediated protection. Wnt activation restored β-catenin activity and fibrosis without significantly changing HMGB1 or TLR4/RAGE/NF-κB signaling (all p > 0.15), a pattern consistent with HMGB1 acting upstream of Wnt/β-catenin. Octreotide limits experimental pancreatic fibrosis by suppressing HMGB1-driven inflammation and downstream Wnt/β-catenin activation, identifying the HMGB1-Wnt/β-catenin axis as a promising anti-fibrotic target.

studies.title: Facilitators and barriers to decentralized Long COVID platform clinical trials using repurposed drugs.
studies.authors: Schito, Marco, Coe, Stacey, Seltzer, Jaime, Davis, Hannah E et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is an emerging chronic condition that results in substantial impairments in quality of life, physical function, and ability to maintain gainful employment. There are no FDA-approved treatments for Long COVID, and recent institution-based clinical trials have not yielded effective treatments. Current standard of care involves trial-and-error drug repurposing that warrants evaluation in rigorous clinical trials. Here we describe potential advantages of decentralized repurposing drug trials as an alternative or complementary approach to institution-based trials. Additionally, we describe lessons learned when launching a local feasibility pilot trial that may inform the design of future decentralized trials in the Long COVID field.

studies.title: Delayed Seasonality but Consistent Age Burden: RSV Epidemiology Pre-, During, and Post-COVID-19 Pandemic on the Kenyan Coast (2008-2026).
studies.authors: Katama, Esther Nyadzua, Maina, Grace, Mutunga, Martin, Lewa, Clement et al.
studies.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic and associated nonpharmaceutical interventions disrupted the established epidemiological patterns of many endemic respiratory viruses globally. However, its impact on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) epidemiology in sub-Saharan Africa is understudied. We analyzed data from a continuous hospital-based pediatric pneumonia surveillance program in coastal Kenya January 2008-June 2026. Children ≤5 years, admitted with World Health Organization-defined syndromic severe or very severe pneumonia were tested for RSV using quantitative reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction. The period was stratified into prepandemic (January 2008-March 2020), during pandemic (March 2020-May 2023), and postpandemic (May 2023-June 2026). Multivariable logistic regression evaluated clinical and demographic shifts across periods. Among 10 374 tested children, 2442 (23.5%) were RSV positive. Positivity declined from 25.3% (1919/7585) prepandemic to 18.3% (235/1282) during the pandemic and 19.1% (288/1507) postpandemic. Overall median age of RSV-positive patients remained statistically consistent across all periods (4.3 vs 3.7 vs 3.1 months; Despite a repeated 1- to 2-month delay of RSV season onsets on the Kenyan coast and minor clinical symptoms shifts, the core demographic patterns remained stable. The persisting severe RSV disease in <6-month-olds highlights this population for RSV interventions.

studies.title: Pulmonary malignant lymphoma requiring surgical lung biopsy for diagnosis following coronavirus disease 2019 infection: a case report.
studies.authors: Akiba, Yoshimasa, Hiraga, Junji, Nakahara, Yoshio, Iwata, Yuya et al.
studies.abstract: Pulmonary involvement by peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (PTCL-NOS), is an exceedingly rare extranodal manifestation with nonspecific radiological and clinical features. Its computed tomography (CT) findings-including ground-glass and consolidative opacities and, in some areas, a crazy-paving appearance-overlap with those of resolving infectious pneumonia and drug-induced lung injury, so that pulmonary lymphoma is readily mistaken for these more common conditions and the diagnosis is often delayed. A 62-year-old man with a smoking history and stage IIIA classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) treated six years earlier with bleomycin-containing chemotherapy-complicated by resolved grade 1 bleomycin-induced interstitial pneumonia-presented with productive cough and low-grade fever after a mild coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) infection. Chest CT showed diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities, with areas of a crazy-paving appearance, together with mediastinal and right hilar lymphadenopathy; the soluble interleukin-2 receptor (sIL-2R) level was markedly elevated (1,540 U/mL). Bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) and transbronchial lung biopsy (TBLB) was non-diagnostic, and the patient deteriorated despite broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy. Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) with wedge resection established the diagnosis of PTCL-NOS, and bone marrow biopsy showed no marrow involvement. Multiple lines of salvage chemotherapy failed to control the disease, and the patient died three months after diagnosis. This case underscores the essential diagnostic role of VATS lung biopsy when bronchoscopic investigation fails in patients with treatment-refractory pulmonary infiltrates. The co-occurrence of prior bleomycin exposure and post-COVID-19 pneumonia created overlapping radiological features that delayed diagnosis. PTCL-NOS should be considered in the differential diagnosis of treatment-refractory pulmonary infiltrates-even when nonspecific patterns such as crazy-paving are present-particularly in patients with a prior history of hematologic malignancy and markedly elevated sIL-2R. The temporal onset of disease following COVID-19 infection in this immunologically predisposed patient further raises awareness of a potential association between severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and lymphomagenesis.

studies.title: Methodological quality and clinical applicability of long COVID guidelines and scientific statements: a systematic review using AGREE II and AGREE-REX.
studies.authors: Montoya Monsalve, Ricardo, Campuzano Cortina, Sofía, Jiménez Cárdenas, Manuela
studies.abstract: Long COVID is projected to affect 0.6 to 1.0% of the population between 2025 and 2030. This study reviewed the methodological quality, clinical applicability and content of the care recommendations issued for adults ≥18 years with long COVID in clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) and scientific statements (SSs). Registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261324906). PubMed, Scopus, trip, five guideline repositories and national health portals were searched between February and April 2026, and PubMed and Scopus were updated on 2 September 2026. Eligible documents were CPGs and SSs on adults with suspected or confirmed long COVID, published in English or Spanish. Screening and full-text review were duplicated independently; data were extracted by one reviewer and verified by a second. Methodological quality was appraised with AGREE II, reporting the six standardised domain scores separately, each rescaled within its domain and never summed into an overall score; applicability was appraised with AGREE-REX. A narrative synthesis covered five predefined care domains. Twenty documents were appraised, 19 from the initial search and one from the update. From the 19 initial documents, 510 recommendations were extracted across five NICE-derived domains, mostly clinical management (63.3%) and care planning (29.6%). Quality was uneven (rigor of development 16.7-97.9%; applicability 0.0-95.8%; editorial Independence median 100%), and only one document reported a GRADE-compatible evidence-to-decision framework. Four documents were prioritised and contributed 99 recommendations; they scored higher than the remaining corpus in all six domains, yet applicability remained their weakest (68%). AGREE-REX showed recommendations directed far more clearly at clinicians than at patients or decision-makers. Content converged on shared decision-making, multidisciplinary rehabilitation, patient-centered care and return-to-work support. Guidance on long COVID is abundant but methodologically uneven, and the unevenness is concentrated in how evidence is linked to recommendations and in applicability. The corpus offers well-formulated clinical content whose evidence-to-decision reasoning and implementation requirements are seldom reported, and it therefore requires formal contextual adaptation, for example through GRADE-ADOLOPMENT, before use. Key limitations are the scarcity of guidance from low- and middle-income countries and the diversity of development methods. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420261324906, Identifier CRD420261324906.

studies.title: Higher risk of Long COVID among patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases and immunomodulatory therapy: a retrospective cohort analysis of national US data.
studies.authors: Singh, Namrata, Anzalone, A Jerrod, Stevenson, Holland, Robinson, Londyn et al.
studies.abstract: Little is known about the prevalence of and factors associated with Long COVID in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases (AIRDs). We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C). We included adults with a first documented SARS-CoV-2 infection between September 2021 and December 2023, with follow-up through December 2024. Long COVID was defined as ICD-10-CM code U09.9 or a Long COVID clinic visit occurring 28 to 365 days after first infection. We compared patients with AIRD with matched non-AIRD controls using 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity score matching on age with exact matching on sex, race/ethnicity, SARS-CoV-2 variant-dominant period, and data-contributing organization. We estimated hazard ratios using multivariable Cox regression models. Among people with AIRD, we assessed risk by AIRD type and medication exposure before acute COVID-19. In the matched cohort of 187,106 patients, Long COVID occurred in 2.8% of AIRD patients and 1.5% among non-AIRD patients. In multivariable analyses, AIRD was associated with an increased risk of Long COVID compared with non-AIRD patients (aHR 1.56, 95% CI 1.45-1.67). Among patients with AIRD, higher acute COVID-19 severity, pulmonary disease, obesity, and exposure to rituximab or glucocorticoids were associated with an increased risk of Long COVID. Sjögren's syndrome was associated with a higher risk of Long COVID. The higher risk of developing Long COVID among AIRD patients compared with those without AIRD underscores the need to identify potential risk factors for Long COVID in this population to minimize its long-term effects.

studies.title: Presence of post-COVID-19 condition in six ethnic groups in Amsterdam, the Netherlands: a retrospectively reconstructed time interval approach.
studies.authors: Spronk, Merve, Boyd, Anders, Campman, Sophie Louise, Jongen, Vita et al.
studies.abstract: In this retrospective cohort study, we assessed the prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) and its determinants among six ethnic groups in Amsterdam, the Netherlands. We analysed data from participants of the HELIUS cohort with SARS-CoV-2 infection who answered questions on the presence and duration of COVID-19-related symptoms between May and November 2022. We estimated the prevalence of PCC, defined as having ≥1 of 15 pre-determined COVID-19-related symptoms remaining for at least 3 months after infection, by ethnicity at several timepoints since infection adjusted for age and sex, and assessed determinants of PCC overall using logistic regression. Of 932 infected participants, 31% [95% confidence interval (95%CI): 27%-37%] developed PCC. At 3 months after infection the adjusted prevalence of PCC varied from 17% (95%CI: 13%-24%) in the Dutch-origin group to 41% (95%CI: 34%-48%) in the South-Asian Surinamese group, and was significantly higher among participants of South-Asian Surinamese, Turkish and Moroccan origin compared to those of Dutch origin (all

studies.title: Post-COVID-19 Patterns of Respiratory Viruses in South African Children With Acute Respiratory Illness.
studies.authors: Barday, Mish-Al, Hulsman, Claire, Mc Gregor, Shawna F, van Niekerk, Margaret et al.
studies.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted respiratory virus epidemiology. We describe the postpandemic prevalence, seasonality and clinical presentation of viral respiratory tract infections (RTIs) among hospitalized South African children. Children 0-<13 years of age with acute RTIs were prospectively enrolled between October 2024 and October 2025. Nasopharyngeal aspirates were collected on admission and tested for 7 common respiratory viruses using a multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction. Clinical, demographic and outcome data were recorded. Disease severity was classified as mild, moderate or severe based on the need for hospitalization, respiratory support, intensive care or major complications. Cluster analysis identified distinct clinical phenotypes. We enrolled 315 children, median age 9.3 months [interquartile range 3.6-24.7, 132/315 (41.9%) female, 7/315 (2.2%) living with HIV and 53/315 (16.8%) HIV-exposed but uninfected. Disease severity was mild in 55 (17.5%), moderate in 184 (58.4%) and severe in 76 (24.1%) children. Respiratory viruses were detected in 276/315 (87.6%); most commonly human rhinovirus (167/276; 60.5%), respiratory syncytial virus (94/276; 34%) and adenovirus (59/315; 18.7%). Respiratory syncytial virus showed strong winter seasonality (P < 0.001), human rhinovirus circulated year-round (P < 0.001) and seasonal Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 activity was low at 10%. HIV exposure (adjusted odds ratio: 3.08)] and viral co-detection (43.5%; P = 0.015) were independently associated with disease severity. Cluster analysis revealed 3 distinct clinical phenotypes of RTIs, with unique symptom profiles, trajectories and virological patterns. Respiratory viruses remained common in young South African children hospitalized with RTIs, with most returning to pre-COVID seasonal patterns and limited Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 activity. Distinct clinical phenotypes identify vulnerable subgroups and underscore the need for improved tools to distinguish severe disease from self-limiting illness.

studies.title: Cognitive assessment of patients with post-COVID olfactory dysfunction and impaired domains.
studies.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
studies.authors: García-Meléndez, David Dylan, Maroto Navas, Daniel, Piernagorda Copado, José, Martín Álvarez, Rocío et al.
studies.abstract: Persistent olfactory dysfunction is a common symptom of post-COVID syndrome (PCS), particularly among younger patients who experienced mild COVID-19. Recent functional neuroimaging studies suggest that persistent olfactory impairment may be associated with cognitive deficits. However, few studies have characterised cognition in this subgroup using standardised neuropsychological assessment. To assess the prevalence of cognitive deficits and their characteristics in patients with persistent post-COVID olfactory symptoms. This multicentre study included 55 patients with PCS and persistent olfactory dysfunction following COVID-19 onset before February 2021. Participants underwent olfactory evaluation using the Sniffin' Sticks test and a comprehensive battery of neuropsychological assessments. The mean age was 43.9 years (SD 10.1), with a mean disease duration of 46.1 months (SD 6.5). According to a domain-based criterion, 67.3% of patients showed cognitive impairment. Domain-specific impairment was observed in attention/working memory (67.3%), executive function (50.9%), and episodic memory (56.4%). The Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) detected abnormalities in only 9.1% of patients. Exploratory comparisons between hyposmic and anosmic patients showed no univariate differences after false discovery rate (FDR) correction, despite a marginal post-hoc multivariate effect. Continuous olfactory performance showed inverse correlations with two executive measures after FDR correction, but no consistent dose-response relationship across cognitive measures. In this selected cohort, a high prevalence of multidomain cognitive alterations was observed. These findings highlight the limitations of brief cognitive screening tools and suggest a complex relationship between persistent olfactory dysfunction and cognition. Further longitudinal studies are warranted.

studies.title: Oral Fluid Inflammatory Biomarker Profile in Long COVID: Evaluation of Oral Active and Total MMP-8, MMP-9, and TIMP-1 in Relation to BMI and Disease Status.
studies.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
studies.authors: Seno Aji, Nur Rahman Ahmad, Thomas, Julie Toby, Tervahartiala, Taina, Räisänen, Ismo T et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID (LC) is characterized by persistent systemic symptoms, but its oral inflammatory profile remains unclear. This study evaluated oral inflammatory biomarkers, particularly matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) -8, -9 and their regulators in oral rinse samples from LC patients. This cross-sectional study analyzed oral rinse samples from 115 LC patients and 103 comparable controls. Periodontal inflammation was screened using a chair-side active MMP-8 (aMMP-8) point-of-care test (POCT). Biomarkers (aMMP-8, total MMP-8, MMP-9, TIMP-1, and MPO) were quantified and validated by Western blotting and gelatin zymography. Associations with LC and clinical variables were assessed using bivariate analysis and multivariable regression. LC patients had significantly higher total MMP-8, MMP-9, TIMP-1, and MMP-9/TIMP-1 ratio (all p<0.05 in both analyses). IFMA-measured active MMP-8 became independently associated with LC after multivariable adjustment. Chair-side aMMP-8 POCT showed a non-significant trend toward higher positivity in LC (16.5% vs. 8.7%). BMI was positively associated with aMMP-8, tMMP-8 and tMMP-8/TIMP-1 molar ratio. Antidepressant use was associated with tMMP-8/TIMP-1 molar ratio. Western blotting confirmed active MMP-8 species and gingipain. These findings suggest an altered oral inflammatory biomarker profile in LC. The potential role of chair-side aMMP-8 POCT for screening oral inflammation in this population merits further investigation.

studies.title: Post-intensive care syndrome at 6 months and 1 year among survivors of severe COVID-19 requiring invasive mechanical ventilation: a single-center observational study.
studies.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
studies.authors: Morimoto, Shinichi, Nakashio, Maiko, Fujita, Akihiro, Maruyama, Junichi et al.
studies.abstract: Long-term multidomain impairment after critical coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) overlaps with post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) and post-COVID-19 condition. We assessed PICS at 6 months and 1 year after hospital discharge and explored associated clinical factors in Japanese patients with COVID-19 requiring invasive mechanical ventilation. This single-center observational study included adult patients with COVID-19 who required invasive mechanical ventilation and survived to discharge. PICS was assessed using the Barthel Index, Short-Memory Questionnaire, and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression examined factors associated with 1-year PICS. Of 67 discharged survivors, 37 completed both 6-month and 1-year assessments; 17 (45.9%) received extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. PICS was present in 22 (59.5%) patients at 6 months and 21 (56.8%) at 1 year, and 15 (40.5%) had cognitive impairment at both assessments. Delirium was more frequent in patients with PICS than in those without at 6 months (63.6% vs 26.7%, p = 0.045) and 1 year (66.7% vs 25.0%, p = 0.020). In the exploratory multivariable analysis, delirium was associated with 1-year PICS after adjustment for age and mechanical ventilation duration (odds ratio, 7.09; 95% confidence interval, 1.54-32.7; p = 0.012). PICS was common 6 months and 1 year after hospital discharge among survivors of severe COVID-19. In an exploratory analysis, delirium was associated with 1-year PICS after adjustment for age and mechanical ventilation duration. This hypothesis-generating finding requires confirmation in larger prospective cohorts.

studies.title: Frequency and correlates of somatic symptom disorder in patients with post COVID-19 condition: Cross-sectional results from the SOMA.COV study.
studies.authors: Reinke, Max, Stein, Clara, Maehder, Kerstin, Toussaint, Anne et al.
studies.abstract: Persistent somatic symptoms are common in patients with post COVID-19 condition (PCC). Yet, somatic symptom disorder (SSD) which captures maladaptive symptom-related thoughts, feelings, and behaviors has not been investigated in individuals with PCC using clinical interviews. This study examined SSD frequency and associated biopsychosocial factors in a randomized controlled trial (RCT) sample of patients with PCC. Baseline data from adults with PCC enrolled in a RCT were analyzed. SSD was assessed using a structured DSM-5-based clinical interview. Self-report measures assessed sociodemographic, disease-related, and psychobehavioral variables. Group differences by SSD status and multivariable associations with SSD were analyzed. Overall, 256 patients with PCC (85.6% female; mean age = 46.8 years, SD = 11.4) completed the baseline assessment, of whom 65.6% (95% CI 59.6%-71.2%) met SSD criteria. Patients with comorbid SSD reported greater functional impairment, more sick leave, and lower mental health-related quality of life, while somatic symptom and fatigue severity did not differ. In multivariable analyses, anxiety severity (OR = 1.11, 95% CI [1.01-1.22]) and negative symptom expectations (OR = 1.27, 95% CI [1.08-1.50]) were independently associated with SSD status. In this sample, SSD was common among patients with PCC and associated with psychological distress and functional impairment rather than somatic symptom severity. Anxiety severity and negative symptom expectations were associated with SSD. Recruitment within a RCT limits the representativeness for the broader PCC population. Routine SSD assessment may help identify a particularly burdened subgroup. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships and mechanisms.

studies.title: Effectiveness of Individualized Physical Exercise in COVID-19-Induced Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome.
studies.authors: Svensson, Annie M, Svensson-Raskh, Anna Um, Törnberg, Anna C, Hallberg, Carl E et al.
studies.abstract: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is common in post-COVID-19 condition and is associated with high symptom burden and reduced quality of life. Although physical exercise is recommended for POTS, evidence of its effectiveness remains limited. The objectives of the study was to evaluate the effectiveness of tailored exercise on health-related quality of life (HRQoL), upright time, physical function, and symptom burden in individuals with COVID-19-induced POTS. Adults with COVID-19-induced POTS were randomized to standard care or standard care plus tailored exercise with weekly supervision. Assessments were conducted at baseline and 16 weeks. Primary outcomes were HRQoL and upright time. Secondary outcomes included daily steps, sedentary time, orthostatic autonomic response, muscle strength, physical capacity, patient-reported activity limitations, mental health, and symptom burden. Analyses used mixed models. Data were analyzed from sixty participants (85% females, mean age 37 years). No time-by-group interaction effects were observed for HRQoL. Upright time was reduced in the intervention group compared with controls, with an estimated between-group difference of -31 min/day, (95% CI -57 to -6). For secondary outcomes, daily steps were reduced in the intervention group, whereas both groups improved in POTS symptoms, activity limitations, and physical capacity, with a trend toward reduced postexertional malaise. No other secondary outcomes showed significant effects. Tailored exercise did not outperform standard care in HRQoL and was associated with reduced upright time, whereas improvements in several secondary outcomes were observed in both groups. Heterogeneity supports an individualized approach to exercise, integrated with pharmacological and multimodal management strategies.

studies.title: "It's quite a dark, long journey to the light at the end of the tunnel": a qualitative study of children's experiences of living with Long COVID.
studies.authors: Alexis-Garsee, Camille, Payne, Nicola
studies.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic had a significant impact on global health, with some individuals experiencing long-term health effects known as Long COVID. This study explored the lived experiences of children with Long COVID, providing further insight into the impacts and needs within this group. Semi-structured interviews, facilitated by children's drawings, were conducted with 15 children. Thematic analysis was used to analyse the data. Four themes were identified: (1) 'I feel completely different': the physical and emotional burden of Long COVID (2) 'Like the buzz of people speaking and I can't concentrate': education challenges created by Long COVID, (3) 'I'm on my third friend group since I've had COVID': disrupted relationships and fractured connections and (4) 'What can I do now to get myself better?': managing life with Long COVID. These findings reveal a narrative of loss and change during key developmental periods. This research illustrates the life-altering impact of Long COVID on children across many domains. Despite these challenges children were hopeful for the future. A multi-faceted approach to management is needed, including utilising technology to aid self-management strategies such as pacing and to support social connection, as well as psychological support and school adjustments.

studies.title: Revisiting What HIV in the Brain Can Teach Us About SARS-CoV-2 Neurological Complications.
studies.authors: Taher, Layan, Arellano, Jekzaly, Al-Harthi, Lena
studies.abstract: In 2021, a Perspective article suggested that principles of HIV neuropathogenesis could provide a conceptual framework for understanding the neurological complications of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection when mechanistic evidence was limited. Five years later, extensive clinical, neuropathological, and experimental studies allow reassessment of that framework. Current evidence has shifted emphasis away from direct viral infection of the central nervous system toward host-mediated mechanisms involving persistent immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, glial activation, thromboinflammation, and disruption of the neuroimmune axis. At the same time, persistent viral antigens and adaptive immune responses, including autoantibodies in subsets of patients, have expanded our understanding of the biological heterogeneity underlying post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection with neurological manifestations. This Perspective revisits the original framework in light of these advances and examines how concepts derived from HIV neuropathogenesis continue to inform our understanding of persistent neurological dysfunction following SARS-CoV-2 infection.

studies.title: Routine laboratory data are decoupled from symptom phenotype and prognosis in Long COVID: within-cohort variation is dominated by age.
studies.authors: Oberhauser, Viola, Perkmann, Thomas, Mucher, Patrick, Quehenberger, Peter et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is defined by persistent multi-organ symptoms without an alternative diagnosis. This study evaluated whether routine laboratory data collected under real-world conditions differentiate symptom-defined subgroups within an outpatient cohort and predict the course. In this single-center cohort study of 564 Long COVID patients (1,452 visits), symptom phenotypes were derived by latent class analysis of 19 organ-system domains at baseline. Structure in 89 routine analytes was sought by k-means clustering, confirmed with alternative algorithms, and repeated after age residualization. Analytes were compared across phenotypes using Kruskal-Wallis tests with false-discovery-rate control and adjustment for confounders. Equivalence testing was performed against reference change values. The course was modeled by count models. Prediction of improvement used a nested cross-validated elastic net with a baseline-independent endpoint. Clustering showed no convincing structure (silhouette ≤0.09, two to eight clusters); the weak split tracked age (50.5 vs. 38 years) and vanished after residualization. Three age-independent phenotypes (n=503) had no laboratory correlate: none of 89 analytes survived FDR correction, with or without adjustment, or across 50 pseudo-class draws. Equivalence held for 86/89 analytes within ±0.5 SD and 63/70 within the reference change value. Symptom burden declined (median 4 to 2 organ systems, p=2.5 × 10 Routine laboratory variation in this cohort was dominated by age and decoupled from symptom phenotype in both directions. Routine testing in a real-world setting could not provide an age-independent diagnostic, subtyping, or prognostic signature in a cohort of patients suffering from Long COVID.

studies.title: Adaptation and Translation of the Brain Fog Scale into the Indian Psycho-Socio-Cultural Context.
studies.authors: Khanna, Himanshi, Panwar, Neeraj
studies.abstract: Brain fog is a subjective experience characterised by forgetfulness, poor concentration, mental slowness, dissociation and fatigue, with individuals describing experiences such as a 'mental wall' over formerly simple tasks. During and after the 2019 pandemic, scientific enquiry into brain fog was revived, explored and studied worldwide. Specifically, a large number of studies focused on the COVID-19 population and established strong associations with long COVID. Further, this in-depth research interest has led to the emergence of brain fog as a transdiagnostic factor. Over the past half-decade, given the said and established facts, the majority of scientific evidence has been contributed by researchers outside India. This highlights that brain fog is subjectively experienced worldwide, but its objective expression varies. Given the existing literature gap, the present article focuses on developing the psychometric properties of the Brain Fog Scale (BFS) and on adapting and translating it into Hindi. For this purpose, a set of data was collected from participants ( Principal component analysis revealed a refined 26-item, two-component structure comprising Psychophysiological Brain Fog (PsyPhyBF) and Cognitive Brain Fog, accounting for 52.8% of the total variance. The adapted scale demonstrated excellent internal consistency, with Cronbach's alpha coefficients of 0.91 and 0.92 for the two components, respectively, and 0.95 for the overall scale. Both dimensions of brain fog demonstrated significant negative associations with QoL, with PsyPhyBF emerging as a significant predictor of poorer QoL. The findings support the reliability and construct validity of the adapted Hindi version of the BFS and highlight the importance of culturally sensitive assessment tools for understanding subjective cognitive experiences in diverse populations.

studies.title: Increased Risk of Thyrotoxicosis After COVID-19 in Adolescents and Young Adults During the Omicron-Predominant Period: A Nationwide Matched Study.
studies.authors: Miyashita, Koichi, Ohba, Kenji, Hozumi, Hironao, Furuhashi, Kazuki et al.
studies.abstract: Thyroid dysfunction has been increasingly reported after the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. To date, no population-based study has examined this association using more than 10 million matched pairs. We compared the risk of documented thyroid outcomes after COVID-19 with that after influenza during the Omicron-predominant period. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the Japanese National Database of Health Insurance Claims, including patients with COVID-19 between January 2022 and March 2023, and those with influenza between September 2017 and March 2023. Individuals with pre-existing thyroid disease were excluded. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 24,173,646 pairs were analysed. Database-recorded outcomes assessed within 90 days of documented COVID-19 infection included diagnoses of thyrotoxicosis, hypothyroidism and subacute thyroiditis, as well as initiation of antithyroid drugs (ATDs) and thyroid hormone replacement therapy (THRT). Among database-recorded outcomes, COVID-19 was associated with higher risks of thyrotoxicosis diagnosis (risk ratio [RR], 1.08), hypothyroidism diagnosis (RR, 1.12), ATD initiation (RR, 1.06) and THRT initiation (RR, 1.22) than influenza, but not subacute thyroiditis diagnosis. Age-stratified analyses showed markedly higher risks in individuals aged 0-19 years for thyrotoxicosis diagnosis (RR, 1.38) and ATD initiation (RR, 1.77). In this nationwide cohort, COVID-19 was associated with higher risks of database-recorded diagnoses of thyrotoxicosis and hypothyroidism than influenza during the Omicron-predominant period. The strongest association was observed for thyrotoxicosis diagnosis and ATD initiation in younger individuals, underscoring the importance of post-COVID-19 thyroid monitoring in adolescents and young adults.

studies.title: Sputum and oral microbiota profiles are associated with long COVID severity and phenotype post-hospitalisation: a UK multicentre, prospective cohort study.
studies.authors: Alferes de Lima Headley, Daniela, Richardson, Hollian, Hennayake, Chandani, Eke, Zsofia et al.
studies.abstract: Acute COVID-19 alters the airway microbiota. Whether these changes persist post-COVID-19 and contribute to long COVID is unknown. We aimed to describe the microbiota by long COVID severity and subtype, and identify links with inflammation. Adults were prospectively recruited to the longitudinal UK Post-hospitalisation COVID-19 study (PHOSP-COVID). Patients were grouped by previously described "severity clusters" (of ongoing health impairments) and symptom subgroups. Oral and sputum microbiota (at 6 months post-discharge) were characterised through 16S ribosomal RNA gene amplicon sequencing, and microbiota diversity was assessed. Co-occurrence network analysis identified keystone taxa. Associations between keystone taxa and plasma inflammatory proteins were assessed through Spearman's rank correlations. 771 participants had their microbiota assessed. Of participants with oral rinses and "severity cluster" assignment (mean age 57.5 years), 278 out of 722 (38.5%) were women. The "very severe" cluster, in which disease was predominantly pulmonary in nature, was associated with a distinct microbiota profile post-COVID-19. Reduced lung function was associated with a distinct oral microbiota profile. Persistent neurocognitive symptoms were associated with a distinct oral microbiota profile, while gastrointestinal symptoms were associated with a distinct sputum microbiota profile. Microbiota keystone taxa shifted to a higher prevalence of lactic acid bacteria associated with worse health outcomes. Lactic acid bacteria abundance was associated with elevated blood inflammatory proteins. Distinct oral and sputum microbiota profiles were associated with pulmonary function and with neurocognitive and gastrointestinal symptoms in long COVID. Shifts in keystone microbiota taxa linked with inflammation, based on worse health outcomes, suggest a potential role change for lactic acid bacteria, which may be associated with the host immune response.

studies.title: Orthopedic Risks and Recovery Considerations in Long COVID: A Narrative Review.
studies.authors: Zelenski, Kyle N, Christensen, Gavin K, Hart, Jeremy, Speth, Jordan C et al.
studies.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic left a lasting imprint on orthopedic surgery, initially through widespread reductions in care delivery and subsequently through the complex challenges posed by Long COVID syndrome. Emerging literature describes Long COVID-related alterations in bone mineral density, delayed wound healing, prolonged inflammation, persistent chronic pain, and increased perioperative risks. Long COVID may adversely affect skeletal integrity through inflammatory, hypoxic, and angiotensin-converting enzyme 2-mediated pathways, potentially leading to bone loss and increased fracture susceptibility. Persistent inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, thrombotic tendency, and neurocognitive impairment may also increase perioperative vulnerability, while chronic musculoskeletal pain, reduced exercise capacity, and post-exertional malaise may complicate rehabilitation and functional recovery. Although orthopedic-specific evidence remains limited, the available findings suggest that Long COVID may represent an underrecognized risk modifier relevant to surgical planning and postoperative management. Greater awareness of these mechanisms may improve patient counseling, risk stratification, and rehabilitation strategies.

studies.title: Exploring the potential benefits of Shirodhara as an add-on therapy for alleviating post-COVID anxiety and depression: A case study.
studies.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
studies.authors: Shamkuwar, Manoj, Pv, Anandaraman, Kataria, Dinesh, Bhatted, Santosh et al.
studies.abstract: In this case study, we present a 31-year-old female, a homemaker, who developed persistent symptoms of anxiousness, fatigue, weakness, irritation, anger issues, and difficulty concentrating for nearly 12 months following recovery from COVID-19. She was diagnosed by a consulting psychiatrist with post-COVID anxiety with depression, and had been on anxiolytic and antidepressant medications for the past ten months. She underwent Shirodhara (dripping of medicated oil on the forehead) using Balashwagandhadi taila for 14 days as an add-on therapy, while continuing her conventional medications. Assessments at baseline, 8th day, 15th day, and 30th day showed progressive improvements: Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A) scores reduced from 42 to 10, Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS) from 23 to 6, Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) from 24 to 1, and Flanagan Quality of Life Scale (QOLS) improved from 59 to 79 by the 30th day. Serum cortisol was 3.09 μg/dL at baseline, below the normal range, and returned to the normal physiological range (11.76 μg/dL) on the 15th day, reflecting improved stress adaptation. C-Reactive Protein remained stable, while Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index showed a transient, non-pathological rise within normal limits. Also, based on the evaluation and recommendation of the psychiatrist, the dosage of conventional medications was reduced: Propranolol was tapered from 20 mg twice daily to once daily, Clonazepam 0.5 mg at bedtime was shifted to as-needed use, and Omeprazole was discontinued. This case highlights the potential role of Shirodhara as an adjunctive therapy in post-COVID anxiety, along with depression. These findings require validation through larger studies with long-term follow-up.

studies.title: Does COVID-19 Vaccination Protect Against Post-COVID Cardiovascular Conditions?
studies.authors: Maria, Lidian Franci Batalha Santa, Naves, Márcio Coutinho Xavier, Duarte, Elisabeth Carmen, Carvalho, Isis Polianna Silva Ferreira de et al.
studies.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases, such as acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, and arrhythmias, have been associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection, representing an important cause of long-term morbidity and mortality. In addition to preventing primary infection, COVID-19 vaccination has emerged as a protective factor against post-COVID cardiovascular outcomes. This study aims to analyse the evidence supporting a causal relationship between COVID-19 vaccination and the prevention of post-COVID cardiovascular conditions, based on classical and contemporary epidemiological criteria, including the Bradford Hill criteria (BHC) and the sufficient component cause (SCC) model. A qualitative synthesis of the evidence was performed according to the nine BHC and the SCC model. Scientific evidence indicates that COVID-19 vaccination meets four of the nine BHC as a protective factor against post-COVID cardiovascular conditions, namely strength of association, consistency, temporality, and biological gradient. Three criteria, biological plausibility, coherence, and analogy, were partially met. Specificity and experimental evidence were not supported by the available literature. The SCC model highlights the fundamental role of vaccination as a preventive causal component. It also contributes to two criteria, strength of association and temporality, while emphasising the limitation of specificity in causal inference. COVID-19 vaccination has proven effective beyond the acute phase of the disease, with protection extending to a reduced risk of post-COVID cardiovascular conditions. Comprehensive immunisation strategies and reinfection prevention are essential to mitigate the burden of post-COVID conditions. Additional studies are needed to explore the underlying biological mechanisms, interactions, and the role of COVID-19 vaccination in preventing post-COVID complications.

studies.title: Insights into the pathophysiology of post-COVID lung disease from the perspective of histopathology.
studies.journal: Pathobiology : journal of immunopathology, molecular and cellular biology
studies.authors: Menter, Thomas, Mertz, Kirsten, Tzankov, Alexandar
studies.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused a broad range of respiratory complications. Among the spectrum of COVID-associated pulmonary conditions, severe bilateral pneumonitis that might progress to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) represents the most critical manifestation. A substantial proportion of survivors of severe COVID-19 continue to experience persistent respiratory symptoms and functional limitations. These findings are referred to as post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). These residual post-COVID lung abnormalities are mechanistically linked to the structural changes of acute lung injury, but also to persistent systemic inflammatory signatures, and are reflected in a range of histopathological patterns, including pulmonary fibrosis, hyperinflammation, angiopathic and immunothrombotic tissue responses. This review focuses on the current knowledge of the pathogenesis and pathophysiology of post-COVID lung disease. We also schematically delineate the broad spectrum of post-COVID lung disease and explain the underlying pathomechanisms.

studies.title: Long-COVID Associated With Incident Hypertension: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
studies.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
studies.authors: Lindberg, Pia, Wiqvist, Samuel, Lee, Seika, Norrman, Anders et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID has been linked to persistent autonomic and vascular abnormalities, but its impact on hypertension among non-hospitalized COVID-19 convalescents remains unclear. Given the link between blood pressure and cardiovascular morbidity, understanding how long COVID modifies the risk of incident hypertension is clinically important. We conducted a longitudinal population-based study using MIRACLE-S (Multimorbidity Integrated Registry Across Care Levels in Stockholm). Adults aged 18 to 65 years without prior hypertension or hospitalization for acute COVID-19 were followed from October 2020 to January 2025. Long COVID was defined by a physician-assigned U09.9 diagnosis. The outcome was new-onset hypertension ( Among 1 221 570 adults, 8365 (0.7%) were diagnosed with long COVID, and 18% developed incident hypertension during follow-up. Individuals with long COVID (women: n=5578, 16%; men: n=2787, 24%) showed an early and consistently higher cumulative incidence than unexposed individuals ( Long COVID was associated with elevated risk of incident hypertension in non-hospitalized COVID-19 convalescents. These findings suggest SARS-CoV-2 infection may contribute to vascular and autonomic dysregulation affecting blood pressure, supporting structured monitoring and risk management in individuals with persistent post-COVID symptoms.

studies.title: Hair cortisol concentration and basal heart rate variability differentiate long COVID from depressive disorders in youth.
studies.authors: Oehlke, S-M, Lozar, A, Goreis, A, Klinger, D et al.
studies.abstract: Depressive symptoms are highly prevalent in long COVID (LC) and may shape its symptom burden. As hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and autonomic nervous system (ANS) alterations have been implicated in both LC and depressive disorders, this overlap raises the question of whether both conditions share psychobiological activity patterns or show distinct profiles. The present study compared these systems between youth with LC and depressive disorders during a developmental period of heightened mental health vulnerability. Thirty-four participants were included (

studies.title: Antiviral Antibody Fc Dysfunction Is Linked to Increased IgG1 Fucosylation in Long COVID.
studies.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
studies.authors: Ukey, Rahul, Michailidis, Ioannis E, Greenberg, Patricia, Andrews, Tracy et al.
studies.abstract: Persistent SARS-CoV-2 antigen is a leading hypothesis for post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), commonly known as Long COVID. Impaired Fc-mediated antiviral antibody function could contribute to inefficient clearance of infected cells and viral antigen despite preserved antibody levels. Therefore, we tested whether PASC is associated with altered Fcγ receptor-mediated antibody function and differences in IgG1 Fc fucosylation, a major regulator of Fc effector function. Serum samples from RECOVER-Adult participants with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection (99 PASC, 139 non-PASC) were analyzed for anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain (RBD) IgG and subclasses, FcγRIIIa- and FcγRIIa-mediated reporter activity as surrogate measures of antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) and antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP), anti-RBD IgG1 Fc glycosylation, and circulating fucose-modifying enzymes. Despite higher anti-RBD IgG and IgG1 abundance, PASC sera showed lower ADCC- and ADCP-associated FcγR reporter activity, including after normalization for antibody abundance. Anti-RBD IgG1 showed greater fucosylation in PASC samples (30 PASC, 34 non-PASC). Serum FUCA2 was lower in PASC samples (24 PASC, 34 non-PASC), whereas FUCA1 and soluble CD16a levels did not differ between the two groups. PASC is associated with impaired antiviral IgG Fc function, increased IgG1 Fc fucosylation, and reduced circulating FUCA2, identifying a glycoimmune axis that may contribute to impaired Fc-dependent antigen clearance and represents a potentially targetable pathway in Long COVID.
